Theme

Money, work & business · Civic life: news, government & the law

economy noun

of a country: its trade, industry and money

also the economy, national economy, recession, state of the economy

modern

M-O s.v. economy
M-O s.v. depression: recession: jacent commercia, we are in a recession

commercia, commerciōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural

the economy

Classically trade and dealings (per commercia et negōtiātōrēs, Tac. Agr. 24); Morgan–Owens extends the plural to a country’s economy. Latin has no classical word for the economy as a whole (see economic).

Other words

  • fidēs, fideī f. — credit, the trust that lending rests on

    noun, fifth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Imp. Pomp. 19: fidem concidisse, credit had collapsed; Caes. BC 3.1.2: cum fidēs tōtā Ītaliā esset angustior

    The Romans spoke of an economy in trouble through its credit: fidēs collapsed (concidit) or tightened (angustior).

Examples

  • haec fidēs atque haec ratiō pecūniārum, quae Rōmae, quae in forō versātur, implicāta est cum illīs pecūniīs Asiāticīs et cohaeret

    this credit, this whole system of money that operates at Rome and in the Forum, is bound up with that money in Asia and hangs together with itCic. Imp. Pomp. 19

  • cum fidēs tōtā Ītaliā esset angustior neque crēditae pecūniae solverentur

    since credit was tighter all over Italy and loans were not being repaidCaes. BC 3.1.2

See also economic, economy, business, money.

SourcesLewis & Short: commercium · Lewis & Short: fides

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. economy; depression: recession.
